RAM samples were prepared with MnZn ferrite volume fractions of 0, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.27, and 0.37.
The MnZn ferrite has a spinel cubic structure with lattice constant a = 8.483 Å.
Densities: MnZn ferrite = 5.029 g/cm³, silicone rubber matrix = 1.28 g/cm³.
Complex permeability (μ = μ' - iμ'') and permittivity (ε = ε' - iε'') increase with ferrite volume fraction.
Real permeability μ' decreases exponentially with frequency, especially above 5 GHz.
Real permittivity ε' is nearly frequency independent; imaginary permittivity ε'' varies complexly with frequency.
Impedance matching condition Z ≈ 1 is required for minimum reflection loss.
Reflection loss (RL) peaks shift to lower frequencies with increasing ferrite volume fraction.
Maximum RL of about -35 dB observed at v = 0.20 and thickness t = 3.0 mm.
Frequency bandwidth for RL < -10 dB at v=0.20 is 4.5 GHz (8.5 to 13.0 GHz).
Increasing thickness generally improves absorption and shifts absorption peak to lower frequencies.
For higher ferrite fractions (v ≥ 0.27), smaller thicknesses may yield better absorption at frequencies ≥ 10 GHz.
Pure silicone rubber (v=0) shows low magnetic and dielectric losses with μ' ≈ 1 and ε' ≈ 3.
SEM images show MnZn ferrite particles with sizes ranging from 1 to 50 μm and varied shapes.
XRD confirms single cubic phase of MnZn ferrite consistent with JCPDS card 74-2401.
Transmission/reflection measurements were performed using an HP 8510C vector network analyzer with APC7 coaxial line.
Reflection loss depends on six parameters: μ', μ'', ε', ε'', wavelength λ, and thickness t.
The dielectric loss tangent (tan δ = ε''/ε') is not constant over frequency or volume fraction.
Mechanical mixing and room temperature curing for 24 hours produced flexible cylindrical RAM samples.
Reflection loss amplitude does not increase monotonically with ferrite volume fraction; it peaks at v=0.20.
